facts.statement: Paleontologist Howard Hutchison discovered the fossil remains of Mirarce in Utah in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1992, in Utah, USA, paleontologist Howard Hutchison discovered fossilized remains of an enantiornithine bird.

facts.statement: Mirarce is a genus of enantiornithine bird from the Late Cretaceous of Utah, named for its meaning of "wonderful winged messenger".
facts.quote: Mirarce (meaning "wonderful winged messenger") is a genus of enantornithe bird from the Late Cretaceous of Utah.

facts.statement: The genus Mirarce contains only one known species, Mirarce eatoni.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, M. eatoni.

facts.statement: Mirarce eatoni was similar in size to a modern Turkey vulture.
facts.quote: It was similar in size to modern Turkey vultures.

facts.statement: Mirarce eatoni grew to be around two feet tall.
facts.quote: Mirarce eatoni was a large turkey vulture-sized bird. It grew to be around two feet tall.

facts.statement: The humerus of Mirarce was short and strong.
facts.quote: The humerus of the bird is short and strong.

facts.statement: Quill knobs, the first such structures ever found in enantiornithines, were preserved on the ulna of Mirarce eatoni.
facts.quote: These elongated folds are located along the length of the bone. Despite the fact that bone fragments do not allow measuring the size of each tubercle, determining the distance between them or estimating the number of secondary feathers, their very presence on the fossil is a very significant fact, as this is the first time the structure has been found in enantiornithines.

facts.statement: Mirarce fossils have been found in the Kaiparowits Formation of western North America from the late Campanian age of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Mirarce fossils have been found in the Kaiparowits Formation of western North America, which dates to the late Campanian age of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Mirarce lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Mirarce is classified as a member of the family Avisauridae, closely related to Avisaurus.
facts.quote: Mirarce was found to be a member of Avisauridae, close to Avisaurus itself.

facts.statement: Mirarce belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
Mirarce is placed within the family Avisauridae.
The genus Mirarce was established by Atterholt et al. in 2018.
